summary: The TypeScript compiles and uses Playwright APIs correctly. All generated test cases map correctly to tests with preserved testCaseIds. However, some selectors are guessed or placeholders (.product-card class) without confirmation these exist on the actual page, and the locator 'role=grid' is assumed without evidence. The selectors 'text=name' and 'text=price' used in TC-002 are likely invalid and too generic; 'text=' selector expects full text or exact match strings, but 'name' and 'price' are placeholders here. Also, in TC-003 navigation validation is weak because it only checks that URL contains /product-detail/, which may not be fully reliable. Await is correctly applied on Playwright assertions. No usage mistakes or asynchronous issues detected.

issues.description: Selectors use placeholder and guessed values such as '.product-card' class and 'role=grid' without verification. The 'text=name' and 'text=price' locators are likely invalid or too generic for selecting product name and price.
issues.recommendation: Confirm actual selectors by inspecting the application under test. Use more specific selectors or text matchers that reflect actual product name and price elements.

issues.description: The navigation assertion in TC-003 only checks if URL contains '/product-detail/', which may be insufficient to confirm correct navigation.
issues.recommendation: Enhance navigation check by verifying page content, heading, or specific identifiers on the product detail page to ensure the correct page loaded.

recommendations: Validate all selector strings against the real web page to avoid brittle or non-functional selectors.
Improve navigation validation by adding assertions on page content after navigation to product detail page.
Consider defining selectors as constants or locators reusable across tests for better maintainability.
